S5.title: What you can and can't bring
S5.retrieval_query: Does the text of the New Zealand Food Bill contain any provision that bans or restricts gardening, and if so, what is the exact wording?

passages.P1:
* Some items are prohibited: you can’t bring or import these into New Zealand.
* Some items are restricted: you need approval to import or export these items.
* You may not be able to bring some medicines or controlled drugs into New Zealand.
passages.P4: To protect our people, environment, and economy, some goods:
passages.P5:
* require a permit
* must be declared
* aren’t allowed into the country at all.
passages.P6: Here you’ll find information on the rules for:
passages.P7:
* medicines
* food, plants, animal products, and other risk items
* weapons
* commercial goods
* other items you might be travelling with.
passages.P9: Prohibited items are not allowed into New Zealand under any circumstances. These items pose a significant risk to our biosecurity, public health, or national security.
passages.P10: You must declare any prohibited items when you arrive in New Zealand.
passages.P11: Bringing in prohibited items is a serious offence and can lead to your arrest.
passages.P13: You need a permit or an exemption to bring these items into New Zealand.
passages.P14: ## Specific rules for what you're bringing into New Zealand
passages.P15: Checking these requirements before you travel will help you:
passages.P16:
* avoid delays
* ensure compliance with Customs and biosecurity regulations
* make your arrival as smooth as possible.
passages.P19: Prescription medicines and controlled drugs (medicines and drugs with strict regulations) have specific requirements. These must be declared on your New Zealand Traveller Declaration.
passages.P21: If you are arriving in New Zealand with prescription medicines (that do not contain controlled drugs), you must:
passages.P22:
* bring a copy of your prescription, or a letter from your doctor confirming you are being treated with the medicine
* keep the medicine in its original packaging
* bring no more than three months of supply
  + You may bring up to six months of supply if the medicine is an oral contraceptive.
passages.P24: You must declare your prescription medicine if either of the following apply:
passages.P25:
* you are carrying more than three months of supply
* the medicine is not prescribed to you or a family member.
passages.P26: Learn more about bringing medicines into New Zealand on Medsafe - this includes guidance on non-prescription medicines.
passages.P28: Controlled drugs are medicines or drugs with strict regulations. If you are arriving in New Zealand with controlled drugs, you must:
passages.P29:
* declare the controlled drugs on your New Zealand Traveller Declaration
* keep the controlled drugs in their original packaging
* bring no more than one month of supply.
* bring either of the following:
  + a copy of your prescription
  + a letter from your doctor confirming both of these:
    - you are being treated with the controlled drugs
    - the name and strength of these drugs
passages.P30: All controlled drugs must be declared on your New Zealand Traveller Declaration.
passages.P31: Find out more about controlled drugs at Ministry of Health
passages.P33: All medicines containing pseudoephedrine are controlled drugs. If you are arriving in New Zealand with medicine containing pseudoephedrine, you must:
passages.P34:
* follow all the controlled drugs declaration instructions
* keep the medicine with you in your hand luggage.
passages.P35: You cannot bring medicines with pseudoephedrine into New Zealand for friends or family.
passages.P36: ### Food, plants, animal products, and other risk items
